subject: cross-lagged panel analysis fit is really bad, and different from the result in mplus

messages.author: 04bcd98c2a7562b9
messages.subject: cross-lagged panel analysis fit is really bad, and different from the result in mplus
parts:
Hello, I have tried cross-lagged panel analysis in R, with lavaan package. 
I did the analysis with Mplus before but I would like to learn how to do it in R. 
The problem is, when I added control variables (which is not an exact term in sem case), the fit got really bad. 

I am making cross-lagged panel analysis with two time measurement, to see how x and y affect each other throughout time. 
When there was no control variables, the code was ;

myModel <- '
x2 ~ x1 + y1
y2 ~ x1 + y1 
x2 ~~ y2
x1 ~~ y1 
'
fit <- sem(myModel, data=dt, missing='fiml', group="group", fixed.x = FALSE) 

and the result is same with the result in mplus. 

However, when I added 'control' variables (c1, c2, c3) at both waves; 

myModel2 <- '
x2 ~ x1 + y1 + c1 + c2 +c3
y2 ~ x1 + y1 + c1 + c2 +c3
x2 ~~ y2
x1 ~~ y1 
'
fit <- sem(myModel2, data=dt, missing='fiml', group="group", fixed.x = FALSE) 


TLI and CFI became really bad and the result is different from the one I got in Mplus. 
What did I do wrong?

The code I used for Mplus was; 
    x2 on x1 y1;
    y2 on x1 y1;
    x2 with y2;
    x1 with y1;
    x2 on c1 c2 c3;
    x1 on c1 c2 c3;
    y2 onc1 c2 c3;
    y1 on c1 c2 c3;
    y1 y2 x1 x2 c1 c2 c3;;

messages.subject: Re: cross-lagged panel analysis fit is really bad, and different from the result in mplus
parts:
This line in your Mplus code appears to contain a typo:
y2 onc1 c2 c3;  
Should there be a space after "on"
--Ed Rigdon
